User Story: As an Account Manager (AM), I want the Customer Since date to reflect the earliest confirmed relationship date, so that account tenure is historically accurate.
Description: The workshop identified inconsistencies in historical tenure dates. The system must calculate the earliest valid engagement date from legacy records rather than relying on record creation timestamps. This ensures executive reporting reflects true customer longevity and prevents misleading tenure data.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. System must calculate Customer Since using earliest valid transaction, contract, or migration record.
2. Value must be read-only for non-admin users.
3. Manual override must require Administrator approval and audit logging.
4. Historical tenure must remain consistent across dashboards and reports.
5. Migration discrepancies must be flagged for review.
Notes: Fixes legacy tenure inconsistencies. Prevents leadership misinterpretation. Requires backend reconciliation during migration.

User Story: As an Account Manager (AM), I want to view recent line items directly in the customer profile, so that I can quickly understand billing activity without deep navigation.
Description: Users expressed frustration navigating multiple levels to view transactions. The system must display recent activity in a summary panel to reduce navigation time and provide immediate context.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Display 20 most recent line items sorted descending by date.
2. Show Date, Product, Description, Amount, Status.
3. Clicking item opens invoice detail.
4. Panel must load under 2 seconds.
5. Respect role-based field visibility.
Notes: Solves being multiple levels deep without context. Requires optimized queries for performance.

User Story: As a Billing Specialist, I want billing preference hierarchy enforced, so that invoices always use the correct payment method.
Description: The workshop emphasized billing inconsistencies when preferences are not clearly prioritized. The system must apply a strict hierarchy to prevent unintended payment methods.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Product-level preference overrides Site and Customer.
2. Site-level overrides Customer-level.
3. If none exist, invoice must fail with descriptive error.
4. Applied level must be logged in audit trail.
5. Inactive billing methods must be blocked.
Notes: Critical to automation. Prevents mischarges. Integrates with Authorize.net tokenization.

User Story: As a Billing Specialist, I want recurring invoices automatically generated, so that manual billing work is eliminated.
Description: Recurring services require consistent billing cycles. The system must generate invoices based on configured schedules and billing hierarchy.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Generate invoice based on configured frequency.
2. Use correct billing preference hierarchy.
3. Prevent duplicate generation in same cycle.
4. Log generation event.
5. Notify billing role on failure.
Notes: Reduces manual workload. Requires background scheduler. Must integrate with decline handling.

User Story: As a Billing Specialist, I want to generate formal credit memos, so that refunds are traceable and compliant.
Description: Credit memos must be formally documented and linked to original invoices for accounting transparency.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Credit memo must reference original invoice ID.
2. Require reason code.
3. Automatically adjust invoice balance.
4. Generate unique identifier.
5. Record audit log.
Notes: Prevents informal adjustments. Syncs with accounting system.

User Story: As a Billing Specialist, I want credit cards stored via tokenization, so that recurring charges are secure and compliant.
Description: The system must integrate with Authorize.net and store only tokens to maintain PCI compliance.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. No raw card data stored.
2. Tokenization required via gateway API.
3. Validate expiration and format.
4. Log addition event without exposing card details.
5. Link token to billing preference.
Notes: PCI compliance critical. Must handle gateway errors gracefully.

User Story: As a Billing Specialist, I want to opt a customer out of recurring automation, so that services can be paused globally.
Description: Customers may require temporary suspension of automation. System must enforce top-level opt-out flag.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Customer record must include opt-out toggle.
2. Block ticket and invoice automation when active.
3. Display warning banner.
4. Log user and timestamp.
5. Override must require confirmation.
Notes: Prevents unintended automation. Integrates with recurring engine.

User Story: As an Account Manager (AM), I want calls grouped by phone number, so that communication history is centralized.
Description: Call logs must be consolidated under correct customer record to prevent fragmented interaction history.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Auto-match calls by caller ID.
2. Display chronological order.
3. Show duration and agent name.
4. Allow manual reassignment.
5. Support search by phone or agent.
Notes: Prevents duplicated outreach. Requires call logging integration.

User Story: As a Customer Success Manager (CSM), I want aggregated margin at customer level, so that profitability is visible at a glance.
Description: Margin must be calculated consistently and reflect all active products and costs.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Calculate margin as (Revenue - Vendor Cost) / Revenue.
2. Support date range filters.
3. Update dynamically on filter change.
4. Flag incomplete vendor data.
5. Match reporting engine totals.
Notes: Must align with Day 2 margin engine. Backend aggregation required.

User Story: As an Account Manager (AM), I want to upload documents to customer records, so that contracts and agreements are centralized.
Description: Document storage must support categorization and secure retrieval.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Support PDF, DOCX, XLSX, images.
2. Require category selection.
3. Store uploader and timestamp.
4. Search by category and filename.
5. Confirm before deletion.
Notes: Prevents reliance on shared drives. Requires secure cloud storage.

User Story: As an Account Manager (AM), I want documents linked to specific sites or products, so that context is preserved.
Description: Documents must maintain relationship to relevant entity.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Allow linking to Customer, Site, or Product.
2. Support multiple entity links.
3. Display entity metadata.
4. Prevent orphan files.
5. Log association changes.
Notes: Ensures audit clarity. Avoid cascade delete issues.

User Story: As an Administrator (Admin), I want admin-only fields restricted, so that sensitive configurations are protected.
Description: Some fields must be restricted to prevent accidental misuse.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Visible only to Admin role.
2. Block direct URL access.
3. Log edits.
4. Display warning when editing.
5. Exclude from standard exports.
Notes: Requires strict role-based access control.

User Story: As a Customer Success Manager (CSM), I want a summarized activity snapshot, so that I immediately understand account health.
Description: Snapshot provides quick operational awareness.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Display Active Sites count.
2. Display Open Tickets count.
3. Display Active Recurring Products.
4. Display Open Invoice balance.
5. Refresh within 5-minute cache window.
Notes: Eliminates deep navigation. Requires aggregate endpoint.

User Story: As a Customer Success Manager (CSM), I want inactive customers blocked from creating new services, so that legacy accounts do not re-enter workflow unintentionally.
Description: Inactive status must cascade logically without deleting history.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Block new Sites and Products when inactive.
2. Stop recurring automation.
3. Show warning banner.
4. Preserve historical records.
5. Log reactivation event.
Notes: Prevents accidental billing. Must cascade logically.

User Story: As an Account Manager (AM), I want historical data validated during migration, so that legacy inconsistencies are resolved before go-live.
Description: Migration must reconcile tenure, billing, and vendor cost inconsistencies.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Detect duplicate legacy IDs.
2. Recalculate margin for historical data.
3. Flag incomplete billing records.
4. Log corrections.
5. Preserve original data snapshot for audit.
Notes: High go-live risk area. Requires data audit script.

User Story: As a Customer Success Manager (CSM), I want low ratings flagged, so that corrective action can be taken proactively.
Description: Reviews must surface performance issues quickly.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Configurable threshold.
2. Visual warning indicator.
3. Filter by rating.
4. Restrict editing to Admin role.
5. Display flagged count on dashboard.
Notes: Supports service quality monitoring.

User Story: As a Billing Specialist, I want to deactivate billing preferences safely, so that obsolete methods are not used.
Description: Inactive billing methods must not affect historical records.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Prevent use if inactive.
2. Preserve historical invoices.
3. Require confirmation before deactivation.
4. Log user and timestamp.
5. Display status clearly in UI.
Notes: Soft delete only. Prevent data corruption.

User Story: As a Customer Success Manager (CSM), I want recurring service tickets auto-created, so that fulfillment remains consistent.
Description: Recurring engine must schedule future tickets reliably.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Support configurable intervals.
2. Generate tickets in advance.
3. Link to product record.
4. Prevent duplicates.
5. Log generation event.
Notes: Requires background job scheduler.

User Story: As a Billing Specialist, I want negative line items allowed for small corrections, so that minor billing errors are handled efficiently.
Description: Not all corrections require full credit memo.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Require reason code.
2. Allow negative value only in adjustment mode.
3. Recalculate invoice total.
4. Lock after posting.
5. Log audit trail.
Notes: Separate from formal credit memo.

User Story: As an Account Manager (AM), I want invoice summary in the profile, so that I quickly assess financial standing.
Description: Invoice summary must give financial visibility without deep navigation.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Show total outstanding balance.
2. Display count of Open and Overdue invoices.
3. Link to invoice detail.
4. Reconcile with accounting integration.
5. Load under 2 seconds.
Notes: Reduces time spent navigating billing module.
